core_obligations: Transfer (S1) (proof lines 3115-3126): given a surjective f_2 : A_2 -> A and objects x_i whose pushforwards become isomorphic over A, lift the situation to F by choosing objects representing the isomorphism classes; the (S1) property of F produces y over A_1 x_A A_2 with the required pushforwards, and its class witnesses (S1) for F-bar.

Set up the second part of (S2) (proof lines 3128-3150): the condition means injectivity of the comparison map from F-bar(A x_k k[epsilon]) to the fibre product over F-bar(k); take representatives y and y' and choose commutative diagrams exhibiting their pushforwards x, x_epsilon, x_0, again over the displayed square of rings.

Conclude with the extra hypotheses (proof lines 3150-3185): given isomorphisms alpha over A, beta over k[epsilon] and the induced gamma over k, one needs the two squares to commute; the left one does by construction, and the discrepancy gamma' arising on the right can be removed when F(k) is a set or a setoid, or by adjusting beta with an automorphism of x_epsilon whose image under the surjection Aut_{k[epsilon]}(x_epsilon) -> Aut_k(x_0) is the inverse of that discrepancy, which is exactly the third listed hypothesis; the (S2) axiom for F then gives the required isomorphism y -> y'.
proof_roadmap: Repeat the (S1) argument verbatim for the associated category in sets.
Reduce the second half of (S2) to the commutativity of two squares built from isomorphisms over A, k[epsilon] and k.
Remove the discrepancy on the right square using one of the three listed hypotheses.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the associated category fibred in sets inherits (S1) from a category cofibred in groupoids, and inherits (S2) provided the category is a predeformation category, or its fibre over k is a set or a setoid, or the automorphism map over k[epsilon] -> k is surjective (statement lines 3094-3113). The proof (proof lines 3115-3188) repeats the (S1) argument for isomorphism classes and reduces the second half of (S2) to removing a discrepancy between two isomorphisms by one of the three hypotheses. H3: an original diagram chase with a genuine choice argument at the end, written out in full.
